summary: This paper presents compiler techniques for Do-loop programs on distributed-memory multicomputers, including a generalized distribution function, a dynamic-programming choice of data layouts across consecutive loops, and pipelining of data guided by dependence vectors. It evaluates two linear-system kernels on a 32-node nCUBE-2 and reports that the dynamic layout and the pipelined version run faster than their alternatives.
why_read: It shows how a compiler can choose data layouts per loop nest and replace broadcasts with pipelining, a compact example of cost-driven data distribution.
main_contribution: A dynamic-programming method that chooses data distributions across consecutive loops, combined with dependence-vector-based pipelining of broadcast-like communication.
main_limitation: The method is restricted to constant data-dependence vectors, one- and two-dimensional arrays and a two-dimensional abstract grid.
evaluation_method: Run times on a 32-node nCUBE-2 comparing dynamic with static layouts for Jacobi iteration and pipelined with broadcast versions for Gauss elimination.
notes: No conflict with the catalog id for title, first author or year (title page: Techniques for compiling programs on distributed memory multicomputers; Pei-Zong Lee; 1995).
